games.altBlowoutCheck: Neither team's most recent game was a 17+ point win (Colts won by 2 vs MIA; Texans lost by 3 @ CLE) — regression check does not apply to either side.
altReasons: Scoring margin: favors Texans — blended PD/g +3.98 (Texans) vs -1.56 (Colts); no major QB change for either team this season (Stroud and Jones have started all of their team's games), so neither side's figure is discounted

Injuries/Lineup (weighted x2 — multi-starter cluster): favors Texans — Colts are without both starting tackles (Jalen Travis OUT - knee, Bernhard Raimann OUT - concussion) and both starting corners are compromised (Charvarius Ward OUT - knee, Sauce Gardner Questionable - calf), plus TE Will Mallory (OUT - hamstring) and DT Jerry Tillery (OUT - calf); Texans' comparable loss is a single starter, DE Danielle Hunter (OUT - hamstring)

Form: favors Texans — both teams are 1-2 over their last three games, but Texans' point differential is +13 over that stretch (L 24-27 @ CLE, W 44-22 @ LAC, L 21-27 vs NYG) vs the Colts' -37 (L 7-42 @ JAX, L 23-27 vs DAL, W 24-22 vs MIA); no QB-change discount applies since both starters played every game in that span

Market: favors Texans — the line has moved further toward Houston as the week progressed (mid-week DraftKings had Colts at roughly +350 / +9.5; CBS Sports' live board now shows Colts +570 / +12.5), consistent with the Colts' worsening O-line/CB injury news

Matchup splits: favors Texans — Colts' makeshift offensive line (both projected starting tackles out) faces a Texans front that, even without DE Danielle Hunter, still returns DE Will Anderson Jr. and DT Foley Fatukasi
Rest: neutral — both teams played Sunday 11/15 and are on the same short Thursday turnaround
Travel: neutral — Colts' trip to Houston is a routine divisional road game, no time-zone/cross-country factor
Motivation/Spot: neutral — AFC South rivalry game, but no clearly verified one-sided motivational edge
Weather/Venue: neutral — Reliant Stadium is a dome, no weather factor
